figures.caption: Figure 5: Impression-level F1 (%) performance across successive memory write-back phases (Base, WB1–WB4) under different structured memory configurations, including episodic memory (E), episodic + visual memory (E+V), and episodic + visual + semantic memory (E+V+S), evaluated on MoE-LLaVA Base (a), Fine-tuned (b), and (c) MoE Fine-tuned backbones.

Figure 1: Conceptual comparison of agent memory- (a) Overwhelmed by massive text tokens (Terranova et al., 2025), (Bonnici et al., 2016); (b) Image-caption pair with immature semantic and episodic structures (Selivanov et al., 2023), (Beddiar et al., 2023); (c) Visual-only methods lacks semantic and episodic structures (Zhang et al., 2022), (Davis et al., 2020); (d) LLM-curated approach with uncontrolled and hallucinated memory (Lin et al., 2025), (Savage et al., 2025); and (e) Bio-Mem (Ours) with 3 persistent memories with efficient retrieval and adaptive routing.

Figure 2: MSM-Mem agent self-evolving architecture- (a) Offline loop- encoding, memory builder, build world memory; and (b) Online loop- run queries, retrieve base and fused writeback stages, accessing fine-tuned foundation model, and adaptive routing.

Figure 6: Impression-level F1 (%) performance across successive memory write-back phases (Base, WB1–WB4) under different structured memory configurations, including episodic memory (E), episodic + visual memory (E+V), and episodic + visual + semantic memory (E+V+S), evaluated on MoE-LLaVA Base (a), Fine-tuned (b), and (c) MoE Fine-tuned backbones.
Figure 7: The comparison of MoE-FT vs. Non-MoE-FT (regular FT) at all memory modalities at best memory phase (WB4).
Figure 3: The impact of writeback phases at best performing memory modality (E, E+V, S+E+V) for MoE fine-tuned (MoE-FT) model. (Here, E = episodic, S = semantic, and V = visual memory).
Figure 4: The impact of continuous memory improvement with writebacks (from base memory to WB4) for MoE fine-tuned (MoE-FT) model.
